label: HS GPA - UC applicants
description: Average high-school GPA of the school's students who applied to UC as freshmen, systemwide. Self-selected applicants only.

label: HS GPA - UC admits
description: Average high-school GPA of the school's students admitted to UC as freshmen, systemwide.

label: HS GPA - UC denied applicants
description: The average high-school GPA (the weighted, capped a-g GPA) of this school's students who applied to UC as freshmen and were not admitted to any campus. Not published directly: it is recovered exactly from the published applicant and admit averages and counts ((applicants x applicant GPA - admits x admit GPA) / denied). Shown only when at least 10 students were denied.
source: UC admissions-by-school data (derived by exact moment subtraction)

label: HS GPA - UC admitted, not enrolled
description: The average high-school GPA of this school's students who were admitted to at least one UC campus but enrolled at none of them - most went to other universities instead. Recovered exactly from the systemwide admit average and the campus enrollee averages, so it appears only when every campus that enrolled the school's students published an enrollee GPA and at least 10 admits did not enroll - a minority of school-years, mostly larger schools.
source: UC admissions-by-school data (derived by exact moment subtraction)

label: HS GPA - UC enrollees
description: Average high-school GPA of the school's students who enrolled at a UC campus, computed as the enrollment-weighted average across the nine campuses (each student enrolls at exactly one).

label: HS GPA - selective-UC applicants
description: The average high-school GPA of this school's applicants to UC's three most selective campuses - Berkeley, UCLA, and San Diego - averaging the three campus figures, each weighted by how many of the school's students applied there. A student who applied to two of the three is counted in both pools. Shown when the pools total at least 10 applications.

label: HS GPA - selective-UC admits
description: The average high-school GPA of this school's students admitted to Berkeley, UCLA, or San Diego, averaging the three campus figures weighted by each campus's admit count. A student admitted to two of the three is counted in both pools. Shown when the pools total at least 10 admits.

label: HS GPA - selective-UC denied
description: The average high-school GPA of this school's students denied at Berkeley, UCLA, or San Diego, averaging the three campus figures weighted by each campus's denial count. Each campus figure is recovered exactly from that campus's published applicant and admit averages, and a campus enters only when it denied at least 10 of the school's students; the pools must total at least 10.
source: UC admissions-by-school data (derived by exact moment subtraction, campus rows)

label: HS GPA - selective-UC enrollees
description: The average high-school GPA of this school's students who enrolled as freshmen at Berkeley, UCLA, or San Diego, weighted by each campus's enrollee count. Each student enrolls at exactly one campus, so nobody is double-counted. Shown when at least 10 enrolled across the three.

label: Admit-denied GPA gap at selective UC
description: At each of Berkeley, UCLA, and San Diego: the average GPA of the school's admitted students minus the average GPA of its denied students; the three campus gaps are then averaged, weighted by applications. A large gap means the campus's decisions cut sharply along the GPA scale within this school; a small gap means its admits and denials carried similar GPAs, so the decisions turned on other things. A campus counts only when both pool averages exist (at least 10 denials there), and the school needs 20+ applications in all.

label: Spread across UC GPA pools
description: The full stretch of average GPAs across every UC pool observed for this school in a year: each of the nine campuses' admitted-student average and denied-student average (pools of 10 or more) is collected, and the measure is the highest minus the lowest. In a typical school the bottom is the average of students denied at the least selective campuses and the top the average of students admitted at Berkeley or UCLA. Needs at least 4 observed pools.

label: UC campuses applied to per applicant
description: How many UC campuses the school's applicants tried, on average: the school's total applications to the nine campuses divided by its count of distinct UC applicants. Runs from 1 (each applicant tried a single campus) toward 9; it has drifted upward over the decades systemwide. Shown when at least 10 students applied.
source: UC admissions-by-school data (campus counts / Universitywide unduplicated count)

label: HS GPA - CSU freshmen
description: Average high-school GPA of the school's graduates who enrolled as CSU freshmen that fall, averaged across campuses weighted by enrollment at each.

label: CAASPP percent met or exceeded, ELA+Math
description: Share of grade-11 students scoring Standard Met or better on CAASPP, averaging ELA and Math (whichever subjects the school has). Census test. Not given in 2020; 2021 participation was far below normal.

label: CAASPP ELA percent met or exceeded
description: Grade-11 ELA, Standard Met or better. Census.

label: CAASPP Math percent met or exceeded
description: Grade-11 Math, Standard Met or better. Census.

label: CAASPP Level 4 share
description: Share scoring Standard Exceeded (the top level), averaging ELA and Math.

label: CAASPP distance from standard
description: Average scale score minus the Standard Met cut (grade-11 ELA 2583, Math 2628), averaging the two subjects. Zero = average student exactly at standard.

label: A-G completion rate
description: Share of the graduating cohort completing the A-G course sequence required for UC/CSU eligibility. Cleaned values; cohorts under 10 dropped.

label: STAR/CST percent proficient or advanced, ELA+Math
description: Share Proficient or Advanced on the CST: ELA grades 9-11 and the pooled high-school mathematics tests, averaged. Census.

label: STAR Math percent proficient or advanced
description: The pooled high-school mathematics CSTs. Census.

label: CAHSEE percent passing, ELA+Math
description: Share of grade-10 students passing the exit exam, averaging ELA and math. Census, but a low bar: strong schools bunch near 100.

label: CAHSEE Math percent passing
description: Grade-10 mathematics section. Census.

label: AP average exam score
description: Average score on all AP exams taken at the school. Self-selected takers; school-years with fewer than 20 exams excluded.

label: AP percent of exams scored 3+
description: Share of exams earning 3, 4 or 5. Same filter as the AP average.

label: SAT average total, 1600 scale
description: Average verbal + math total of the school's SAT takers on the pre-2006 1600-point scale. Not comparable to the 2400-scale series.

label: SAT average total, 2400 scale
description: Average reading + math + writing total on the 2006-16 era 2400-point scale. Not comparable to the 1600-scale series.

label: SAT percent meeting both benchmarks
description: Share of takers meeting the College Board benchmark in both sections. Published two years only.

label: ACT average composite
description: Average composite of the school's ACT takers. Published through 2012-13.

label: ACT percent scoring 21+
description: Share of takers at or above 21.

label: CSU GPA one year after entry
description: Average college GPA at CSU one year in, for the school's CSU freshmen. Source rounds each school-by-campus cell to one decimal before averaging.

label: Math readiness at CSU entry
description: Share of the school's CSU freshmen who had fulfilled the GE math/quantitative-reasoning requirement before entry or placed into the course with no supported instruction. The remainder needed supported instruction (remediation). School-years with fewer than 10 CSU freshmen excluded.

label: Writing readiness at CSU entry
description: Same as math readiness, for the GE written-communication requirement.

label: UC Entry Level Writing Requirement met
description: Share of the school's UC enrollees who had satisfied UC's writing requirement when they enrolled.

label: UC one-year retention
description: Share of the school's UC freshmen still enrolled one year later, systemwide.
source: UC graduation-rate data by high school

label: UC four-year graduation
description: Share of the school's UC freshmen graduating within four years, systemwide.
source: UC graduation-rate data by high school

label: UC six-year graduation
description: Share of the school's UC freshmen graduating within six years, systemwide.
source: UC graduation-rate data by high school

label: Unduplicated pupil percentage (student need)
description: The share of the school's students who are low-income, English learners, or in foster care, counted once each - the state's own measure of concentrated student need, from the CUPC collection each October. This is the need figure UC and the state both use administratively. Available for 2017-25 school years.
source: CDE CUPC collection (via the project's upp_lcff component)

label: LCFF+ designation (need of 75% or more)
description: Whether the school carries UC's LCFF+ designation, which switches on when the unduplicated pupil percentage reaches 75%. Shown as 1 for designated schools and 0 for the rest. The threshold is a sharp administrative line rather than a description of the school, which is exactly what makes it useful: schools just above and just below it are otherwise very similar. Available for 2017-25.
source: CDE CUPC collection; UC's LCFF+ rule (UPP >= 75)

label: Socioeconomically disadvantaged share (grade 11)
description: The share of the school's grade-11 students reported as socioeconomically disadvantaged, taken from the enrollment counts published alongside the CAASPP results. Measured on the tested grade rather than the whole school. Available 2016-25; not given in 2020.
source: CAASPP research files, per-group reported enrollment

label: English learner share (grade 11)
description: The share of the school's grade-11 students classified as English learners, from the enrollment counts published alongside the CAASPP results. Available 2016-25; not given in 2020.
source: CAASPP research files, per-group reported enrollment

label: Under-represented minority share
description: The share of the school's grade 9-12 enrollment that is Hispanic, Black, or American Indian - the University of California's definition of under-represented groups. Measured on the school's own students, not on the surrounding neighborhood. School-years with fewer than 20 students enrolled are hidden. Available 2014-25.
source: CDE per-school enrollment by race/ethnicity, grades 9-12

label: Neighborhood median household income
description: The median household income of the census tract the school building sits in, from the American Community Survey. ⚠ This describes the neighborhood around the school, NOT the families of its students - magnets, commuters, and attendance boundaries pull the two apart, sometimes drastically. Compare it against the need measures rather than treating it as one of them. Available 2015-25; not given in 2020.
source: American Community Survey 5-year estimates, school tract

label: Charter school
description: Whether the school is a charter school (1) or not (0), from the California Department of Education public school directory. Treated as fixed over the whole period. Stored in schools.csv rather than the panel, since it does not vary by year.

label: School size (students per grade)
description: The approximate number of students per grade, used elsewhere on the page for the size-weighted trend line. Treated as fixed over the whole period. Stored in schools.csv rather than the panel, since it does not vary by year.
source: CDE enrollment (grades 9-12, divided by four), with fallbacks
